Bahrain End of Service Gratuity Calculator

Enter your last wage and your service dates to see your gratuity and who pays each part.

Calculate your gratuity

Basic salary plus social allowance, if any.

Bahrain gratuity rules

  • Rate: half a month's wage for each of the first three years, then a month for each year after.
  • Wage: the last wage, meaning basic salary plus social allowance.
  • Resignation: no reduction; no minimum and no cap.
  • Who pays: the employer for service before 1 March 2024, the Social Insurance Organization for service since then.

Example: last wage BHD 700 and 5 years of service. First three years: 3 × 0.5 = 1.5 months; two more years: 2 months; total 3.5 months = BHD 2,450.

Frequently asked questions

How is end-of-service gratuity calculated in Bahrain?

Half a month's wage for each of the first three years of service and a full month's wage for each year after, on the last wage (basic salary plus social allowance), under Article 116 of Labour Law 36/2012 and Article 9 of Decision 109/2023. There is no minimum, no cap and no reduction for resignation.

Who pays the gratuity in Bahrain since 2024?

Since 1 March 2024, the Social Insurance Organization pays the part of the gratuity for service from that date, funded by employer contributions. The employer pays the part for service before 1 March 2024.

Does resignation reduce the gratuity in Bahrain?

No. The gratuity is not reduced when the worker resigns.

How do I claim the SIO part?

The SIO part is requested through the organization's website after the end of service, and it cannot exceed the contributions paid for you.

Sources

  • Prime Minister's Decision No. 109 of 2023 on end-of-service benefits for non-Bahrainis — Legislation and Legal Opinion Commission (Arabic)
  • Labour Law for the Private Sector 36/2012 (official translation) — LMRA: Articles 47 and 116
  • EY — Bahrain implements new end-of-service benefit system from 1 March 2024
